subject: Post-demo: Load test coordination & SLOs (FinWise)
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Alex Porter <alex.porter@finwise.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@finwise.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-18T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: Load test coordination & SLOs (FinWise)

Alex/Priya — thanks again for your time today. Great demo discussion — as promised, putting next steps here so we can get the customer-led load test scheduled and scoped.

Key SLOs you mentioned on the call (please confirm):
- P95 latency target: <= 250 ms (for 1k req/s steady state)
- 99th percentile tail: ideally < 500 ms
- Throughput target: 1,000 req/s sustained for 15 minutes / bursts to 1,500 req/s
- Concurrency: ~200 concurrent connections
- Streaming: partial responses required for incremental updates; client keeps a persistent connection per session

What we need from FinWise to proceed:
1) Confirm the above SLOs (or provide exact numbers you want validated).
2) Provide IP ranges to allowlist for the load test or confirm Redwood will use the below ranges.
3) Confirm a test account (API key / test org) we can use; if you need us to create a test user, confirm scope (read/write).
4) Preferred load test windows (we suggested: 3/22 00:00-04:00 PT or 3/23 02:00-06:00 PT).
5) Any egress/cost constraints or rate-limiting behavior we should model.

Attachments: I've attached a sample k6 script (finwise_k6_script.js) and our runbook (loadtest_runbook.pdf) — both are drafts and meant to be iterated with your SRE.

Next steps / owners:
- Alex: confirm SLOs + test window preferences (by 3/19 EOD)
- Priya: share allowlist IPs and whether you want us to use a dedicated test org or create temporary API keys (by 3/19 EOD)
- Logan: will prepare the k6 scenario and environment; will reply with exact IPs and token scopes required.
- Marissa: will be on-call during the run for any infra issues.

Thanks — excited to get this scheduled.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: finwise_k6_script.js (k6 script), loadtest_runbook.pdf (runbook)
From: Alex Porter <alex.porter@finwise.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finwise.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-18T15:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Load test coordination & SLOs (FinWise)

Thanks Laura — appreciate the clear summary. Confirming the SLOs we want validated:
- P95 latency: <= 200 ms (we’d like to be conservative)
- P99 latency: < 450 ms
- Sustained throughput: 1,200 req/s for a 10-minute window, with a 2-minute ramp up/down.
- Peak bursts: 1,800 req/s for short bursts (<= 60s).
- Concurrency: target 250 concurrent long-lived streaming sessions (clients keep connections open to receive partial responses).

Test windows: 3/23 02:00-06:00 PT works best for our infra team.

Allowlist/IPs: attaching the internal list in a follow-up from our network team — will share by EOD tomorrow.

Test account: we prefer Redwood to generate a dedicated test org and test API keys that we can rotate after the run. Scope: full read/write but limited to test data only.

Notes/questions:
- For streaming, we rely on chunked partials — do you have a recommended client behavior for reconnects/timeouts?
- Can you confirm whether Redwood’s rate-limiting will apply per API key or per IP during the test?

Alex
Head of Platform 
FinWise
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Alex Porter <alex.porter@finwise.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@finwise.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-18T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Load test coordination & SLOs (FinWise)

Alex — thanks for the specifics; those targets are helpful. Quick technical notes and ask from Redwood SRE side: 

Planned approach:
- We'll run a customer-led k6 script (attached draft) from our orchestrated load generators. Script supports both HTTP streaming (Server-Sent Events / chunked) and non-streamed requests; we’ll parameterize for both.
- Ramp plan: 2-minute linear ramp to target, hold for 10 minutes, 2-minute linear ramp down. We'll run a 3x warmup at low rate before measurement window.
- Observability: we’ll push detailed telemetry to your team (p95/p99, p50, error rates, connection counts, backend CPU/memory markers if you share access).

IP allowlist / networking:
- Recommended Redwood load generator IPs (please allowlist these): 34.120.45.0/24, 34.120.46.0/24, 35.185.128.0/24
- If you prefer to only allow a single CIDR, we can consolidate to 34.120.45.0/22 but that requires coordination with infra.

Rate limit behavior:
- During tests we can disable multi-tenant rate limiting for the dedicated test org; however, internal infra protections (per-node connection caps) remain. We’ll provision isolated capacity for the run to avoid cross-tenant impact.

Credentials:
- Laura: can you confirm creating a test org and API keys? If you prefer, we can generate the keys and share via a secure link (DocuSign/1Password shared item).

Attachments: finwise_k6_script.js (draft) — contains parameters for concurrency, streaming flag, ramp durations.

I’ll be on the test call; Marissa will handle infra-side monitoring and fallback steps.

— Logan Wright
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finwise.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Alex Porter <alex.porter@finwise.com>
Date: 2027-03-18T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Load test coordination & SLOs (FinWise)

Thanks everyone — quick confirmations from our side:
- We will allowlist the three CIDRs Logan listed for initial testing. Our infra team will confirm the exact entries in the firewall by EOD 3/19.
- Test window confirmed: 2027-03-23 02:00-06:00 PT. We’ll reserve the slot but will send a final go/no-go 24 hours prior.
- We prefer Redwood to create the test org/API keys and share them via 1Password. Scope: read/write limited to test namespace; please delete or rotate keys after the run.
- Our security/compliance team requires an abbreviated evidence packet post-run (logs, runbook, and any exception notes). Can Redwood provide that?

Also: for streaming reconnect behavior — our client will implement exponential backoff with jitter, max 3 retries before marking a session as failed for the test metrics. Please let us know if that’s compatible with how you’ll measure session success.

Priya Shah
SRE Manager, FinWise
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Great — thanks for the quick confirmations. Consolidating next steps and owners: 
- FinWise (Alex/Priya): share final allowlist entries (CIDRs) and confirm go/no-go 24h before run (owner: Priya) — due 2027-03-22 02:00 PT.
- Redwood (Laura/Logan): create test org and generate API keys; share via 1Password and include key rotation instruction (owner: Laura) — keys delivered by 2027-03-19 12:00 PT.
- Redwood (Logan/Marissa): finalize k6 script parameters (concurrency=250, streaming=true, ramp/hold timings as discussed), validate scripts against a small-scale smoke run on 3/22 18:00 PT.
- Redwood (Marissa): produce the post-run evidence packet (logs, runbook, summary of exceptions) and send to FinWise security (owner: Marissa) — deliverable within 48 hours post-run.

Please reply if any dates/owners need adjustment. Otherwise, I’ll mark these in our HubSpot deal and schedule the smoke run and main run invitations.

Thanks again — looking forward to the run.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
